profiles.title: Your profile for German recruiters
profiles.lead: Recruiters in Germany search LinkedIn and XING by job title, skills and location. Work through the checklist so that your profile turns up in those searches and holds up when someone opens it.

intro.linkedin: LinkedIn is the network most international employers in Germany use to find candidates. A complete profile is also what recruiters open after reading your application.
intro.xing: XING is the professional network of the German-speaking market. Many medium-sized companies and German recruiters still search here.

profiles.lockTitle: The Free plan shows the basics.
profiles.lockText: The full checklists for LinkedIn and XING, with examples and message templates, are included from the {{plan}} plan.

visa.title: Documents for your visa route
visa.lead: Tick off what you already have. The list covers the documents that follow from the law. Your mission abroad may ask for further formalities, which you will find on its website.

firstDay.title: From job offer to your first day
firstDay.lead: You have the contract. What follows is a series of steps that build on each other: visa, a place to stay, the move, and the paperwork in your first weeks. Tick them off as you go.
firstDay.callTitle: Want an overview of your next steps?
firstDay.callText: In the Germany Immigration Call (€59) we go through your situation and the official sources together.

signals.tipText: You can start work in Germany while your qualification is still being recognised. You agree to apply for recognition right after arrival, and the employer lets you complete the qualification measures the recognition authority requires as part of your job. You need a concrete job offer, at least sufficient German and a state-recognised qualification from abroad: vocational training of at least two years or a university degree.

lists.noMatch: No entries match these filters. Change a filter to see more.

boards.title: Where to search, by field
boards.lead: The general boards cover every industry. The specialised ones are often less crowded and closer to the right employers.
boards.lockTitle: The Free plan shows the general boards.
boards.lockText: Boards by industry and field are included from the {{plan}} plan.

agencies.title: Recruitment agencies: how they can help
agencies.lead: Agencies know employers who are hiring before the job ad goes online, and some specialise in candidates from abroad. Before you register, you should know which kind of agency you are dealing with.
agencies.lockAll: How agencies work, what to watch out for with your visa, how to apply through them and a list of agencies. Specialised agencies with filters are part of Plus.
agencies.lockSomeTitle: Starter shows the large generalist agencies.
agencies.lockSome: Specialised agencies by field, with filters for the way they work and for recruiting from abroad, are included in the {{plan}} plan.

companies.title: Companies that hire internationally
companies.lead: Employers that show signs of hiring from abroad: job ads in English, relocation support on the careers page or in job ads, or a visa process run by the employer. Each signal comes with the date we last checked it.
companies.note: A signal shows that a company has hired from abroad or says it does. It is not a promise that it will hire you.
companies.lock: Companies with signs of international hiring, filtered by industry and signal, with a link to each website.

jobs.title: Current jobs for international candidates
jobs.lead: Job ads written in English or mentioning relocation, visa support or a recognition partnership, collected from job boards and company careers pages. Ads for temporary agency work are left out.
jobs.fieldNote: Filtered for your field: {{field}}. Change the filter to see all jobs.
jobs.added: Added to your applications as Planned, with a reminder in three days.
jobs.note: The ad itself always opens on the original site. Ads are removed when they go offline or after 30 days.
jobs.lock: Current job ads for international candidates, with filters and a direct link to the ad. One click adds a job to your applications.

german.title: German for applications and interviews
german.lead: The phrases you need for the cover letter, the phone call and the interview, plus the vocabulary of your field. Each with the English meaning and when to use it.

intro.cover_letter: A German cover letter is formal and short. These phrases cover the parts every letter needs.
intro.phone: Phone calls are where many candidates lose confidence. Prepare the opening and the two or three sentences you will need.
intro.interview: Interviews in Germany are structured and fairly direct. These phrases help you describe your experience and ask your own questions.
intro.vocabularyOwn: Terms you will hear in job ads and interviews in your field.
intro.vocabularyGeneral: Set your field under Account settings to see the vocabulary for your profession.

german.lock: The Free plan shows the phrases for the cover letter. Phone call, interview and the vocabulary for your field come with Starter.

knowledge.title: Interviews and the complete guide
knowledge.lead: How job interviews in Germany are structured, and the full contents of the guide Land your first job in Germany to read online.
knowledge.lock: Interview preparation and the complete guide to read online.

contract.title: Your employment contract, explained
contract.lead: German employment contracts use terms that are not obvious, even with good German. This page explains what the common clauses are about, so that you know what to look for before you sign.
contract.generalText: This page explains common terms. We do not review individual contracts.
contract.lock: Probation period, notice period, fixed term, working hours and overtime, holiday, pay and collective agreements, explained in plain language.

overview.leadFirst: Good to have you here. This portal is here to help you turn your plan into reality: a job in Germany and a good start in your new home. The best way to begin is to bring your CV into German format and then set up your LinkedIn profile. Your next steps below show you the way.
overview.lead: Start with your CV and your LinkedIn profile, then keep track of your applications and the documents for your visa route.
overview.fieldTitle: Which field do you work in?
overview.fieldText: We use it to filter jobs, companies and agencies for you. You can change it at any time under Account settings.
overview.fieldSaved: Saved. Jobs, companies and agencies are now filtered for {{field}}.
overview.nothingOpen: Nothing open right now. New steps appear here when a follow-up is due or new jobs come in.

apply.label: Apply
apply.hint: Send your application by this date. Earlier is better, job ads can go offline without notice.

follow_up.label: Follow up
follow_up.hint: If you have not heard back by this date, send a short email asking about the status. The template is under CV and cover letter.

interview.label: Interview
interview.hint: Prepare with the interview guide and German for the job. You get a reminder by email the day before.

documents.label: Send documents
documents.hint: The employer has asked for further documents. Send them by this date.

decision.label: Ask about the decision
decision.hint: If you have not heard back after the interview by this date, ask politely about the timeline.

offer_reply.label: Reply to the offer

none.hint: This application is closed. You find it in the history of the application.
